issue: PMAT-230 — the v1.28.0 release was blocked at release.yml's dist-artifacts job by `/tmp/SHA256SUMS already exists`, a file left by a previous release on a clean-room runner that is not ephemeral. All three `gh release download` call sites now pass --clobber (never --skip-existing, which would exit 0 leaving the PREVIOUS release's checksums for `forjar dist --checksums-file` to embed in install.sh), and the two other fixed /tmp paths release.yml writes into are cleared before they are written: /tmp/dist-output, whose whole contents are uploaded as the release's artifact, and /tmp/tap, where `git clone` exits 128 over an existing directory. Rules 9 and 10 of the workflow shape test hold both properties.
recorded_at: after three review rounds and the twelve-case mutation battery, before the push

quorum.rounds: three, each on a different commit with the base pinned at b3e5812d: 469cc9a9 (0/3 PASS), b02d26b4 (1/3 PASS), 5d1920f6 (0/3 PASS). NO ROUND PASSED and none is claimed to have. Each round refuted the RULE, never the workflow fix; every refutation that reproduced was closed and measured before the next round.
quorum.kill_rule: a lane could fail the whole change on one refuted claim and eight of nine did. Every refutation was re-run by the orchestrator: the ones that reproduced became mutation cases in docs/audits/logs/PMAT-230-rule9-mutations.log, and the two deliberately not acted on are named in the digest with the reason. What closes the ticket is the twelve-case battery and the red/green pair, not a green lane — and the battery caught a defect in the rule that no lane found (cutting the joined command at a bare `|` also cut it at `||`, disarming the suppressed-failure assertion).
refuted_claims: Round 3, as worded: 'rule 9 finds a call site by reading gh's grammar' — refuted 3/3. It read `release` as any token after `gh`, so `gh api --pattern release download` was flagged, and it did not skip a flag's value when looking for the subcommand. Corrected: `release` must be gh's own subcommand (first non-flag token after `gh`, with -R/--repo and their value skipped) and the subcommand the first non-flag token after that; battery case 9 is the lane's counter-example and leaves the rule green, case 1 keeps `gh release -R repo download` red.

Round 3, as worded: 'the rule's comment names what it cannot catch' — refuted by one lane: two commands separated by `&&` or `;` on one continued line were neither caught nor admitted, and the second's flags were read as the first's. Corrected: joined_command cuts at the first `&&` or `;` (and NOT at a bare `|`, which would disarm the `||` assertion — measured), and the comment now names the shell forms that remain outside the ratchet.

crux.verdict: accept(the surveyed release systems make this defect unreachable rather than guarded: a Kubernetes release job runs on an ephemeral pod whose filesystem does not survive it [X], Bazel's actions execute in a sandbox whose inputs are declared and whose outputs are the only thing that leaves [X], a Nix builder gets a fresh store path per derivation [X], and SLSA's whole premise is a build whose environment is reproducible and not carried over between runs [X]. forjar's clean-room runners are long-lived by design — that is what makes them a clean room for THIS repository's binaries — so the property those systems get from ephemerality has to be written down, and the two rules here are where it is written. No new CRUX row is due: this release's behaviour paragraphs are already reconciled in docs/audits/crux-1.28.0.md and this change adds none.)
